headline: Thanksgiving break: 15 family-friendly Treasure Coast events for Nov. 21–29
subhead: From Manatee Fest and outdoor movies to a Thanksgiving Turkey Trot and holiday tree lighting, here are nine days of local activities for families.
teaser: Fifteen family-friendly Treasure Coast events Nov. 21–29, including Manatee Fest, nature walks, a movie at Tradition, a Turkey Trot and Stuart's Christmas on Main Street.
body:
School is out for Thanksgiving break, and families across the Treasure Coast have nine days to fill before classes resume. From a manatee celebration and a movie under the stars to guided nature walks, a Thanksgiving morning 5K and the first big Christmas festivities, there is plenty to do without traveling far.

Here are **15 family-friendly picks for Saturday, Nov. 21, through Sunday, Nov. 29**, drawn from Treasure Coast Today's events calendar. The schedule includes free activities and ticketed experiences, with options for little kids, teens and adults. The selections are arranged by date so families can plan around Thanksgiving itself.

## 1. Manatee Fest in Fort Pierce

**When:** Saturday, Nov. 21, 10 a.m.–2 p.m.. **Where:** Manatee Observation and Education Center, 480 N. Indian River Drive, Fort Pierce. **Admission:** Free for this event.

Start the break with a celebration of the Indian River Lagoon's best-known marine mammal. The center is advertising free admission for Manatee Fest, along with games, activities, cake and face painting. It's an easy pick for young children, especially families who want something educational that still feels like a Saturday outing.

[Event details](https://manateecenter.org/event/manatee-fest/).

## 2. The Market at Newfield Farm in Palm City

**When:** Saturday, Nov. 21, 9 a.m.–1 p.m.. **Where:** Newfield, 1050 SW Prairie Avenue, Palm City. **Admission:** Check organizer for individual activities and purchases.

Local vendors, fresh food, live music, food trucks and activities for kids make this more than a quick shopping trip. The monthly farm market offers a relaxed way to spend the morning, eat lunch outside and give the whole family somewhere to wander before the holiday week begins.

[Event details](https://discovermartin.com/event/the-market-at-newfield-farm-2/2026-11-21/).

## 3. Port St. Lucie International Fest

**When:** Saturday, Nov. 21, 5–9 p.m.. **Where:** MIDFLORIDA Event Center, 9221 SE Event Center Place, Port St. Lucie. **Admission:** Free admission; food available for purchase.

The city's celebration of world cultures brings international food, entertainment, exhibits and vendors together for an evening festival. Live music is planned, and organizers are encouraging visitors to bring nonperishable food donations for the Treasure Coast Food Bank. For families with older children, this is a chance to sample new flavors and experience different traditions without leaving town.

[Event details](https://www.cityofpsl.com/Events/Special-Events/Port-St.-Lucie-International-Fest).

## 4. Sunday Snake Brunch in Hobe Sound

**When:** Sunday, Nov. 22, 12:30–1 p.m.. **Where:** Hobe Sound Nature Center, 13640 SE Federal Highway, Hobe Sound. **Admission:** Free.

It's not a traditional brunch. The nature center's weekly snake-feeding demonstration lets children watch reptiles up close while learning about their behavior and ecological role. The short program is an especially convenient stop for families looking for a memorable activity that doesn't take up the entire afternoon.

[Event details](https://discovermartin.com/event/sunday-snake-brunch-3/2026-11-22/).

## 5. Sea Turtle Season Recap Beach Walk in Stuart

**When:** Monday, Nov. 23, 9–10:30 a.m.. **Where:** Bob Graham Beach, 4774 NE Ocean Boulevard, Stuart. **Admission:** Free; advance reservation required.

Take a guided walk on the sand while learning which sea turtle species nest locally, how nesting works and what happened during the 2026 season. Organizers say the walk covers roughly three-quarters of a mile to one mile. Children must be accompanied by an adult; bring water, sun protection and appropriate footwear. Reservations and waivers are required, and pets are not permitted.

[Event details](https://discovermartin.com/event/2026-sea-turtle-season-recap-beach-walk/).

## 6. Bug Buddies at the Hobe Sound Nature Center

**When:** Tuesday, Nov. 24, 10–10:30 a.m.. **Where:** Hobe Sound Nature Center, 13640 SE Federal Highway, Hobe Sound. **Admission:** Check organizer for admission details.

Bugs get their turn in the spotlight during a short nature program about the tiny creatures that keep Florida ecosystems running. Children can explore how insects and other small animals survive and adapt. It's a particularly approachable choice for younger wildlife enthusiasts.

[Event details](https://discovermartin.com/event/bug-buddies/2026-11-24/).

## 7. Cinema Night at Tradition

**When:** Tuesday, Nov. 24, 5:30–8 p.m.; movie begins at 6 p.m.. **Where:** Grass area across from the Tradition Gazebo, Port St. Lucie. **Admission:** Check organizer; popcorn and light bites available for purchase.

An outdoor screening of *GOAT* gives families an easy Tuesday-night plan. Bring chairs or blankets (organizers recommend a liner underneath), settle in on the grass and enjoy the movie under the evening sky. The organizer asks attendees to RSVP through its event page.

[Event details](https://traditionfl.com/events/cinema-night/).

## 8. Guided Full Moon Hike at Jonathan Dickinson State Park

**When:** Tuesday, Nov. 24, 6–8 p.m.. **Where:** Meet at the Kimbell Center, Jonathan Dickinson State Park, Hobe Sound. **Admission:** Program free with park admission; reservation required.

Families comfortable walking trails after dark can experience the park in an entirely different setting on a guided hike under the Beaver Moon. Bring a flashlight and insect repellent. Space is by reservation; call **561-745-5551** before going. This is a better choice for children who can manage an evening walk than for families with very young kids.

[Event details](https://discovermartin.com/event/guided-full-moon-hike/).

## 9. Tales and Scales: Alligator Encounter

**When:** Wednesday, Nov. 25, 10–10:30 a.m.. **Where:** Hobe Sound Nature Center, 13640 SE Federal Highway, Hobe Sound. **Admission:** Free.

Meet the nature center's young alligators, Marsh and Meadow, and learn about the adaptations that let these reptiles thrive in Florida. The presentation also explains why alligators matter to the habitats they share with other wildlife. It's a short, educational stop that leaves most of the day open for holiday preparations.

[Event details](https://discovermartin.com/event/tales-and-scales-alligator-encounter-3/2026-11-25/).

## 10. Hike With Goats in Palm City

**When:** Wednesday, Nov. 25, 4:30–5:30 p.m.. **Where:** KC Trails, 100 SW Newfield Parkway, Palm City. **Admission:** Listed at $20–$25.

For a less typical outdoor adventure, KC Trails has scheduled a guided walk with friendly goats along its trails. The animal companions and scenic route make this one of the week's more unusual choices. Check age guidelines, ticket availability and what to wear with the organizer before booking.

[Event details](https://discovermartin.com/event/hike-with-goats-4/).

## 11. Tradition Turkey Trot 5K

**When:** Thursday, Nov. 26 — Thanksgiving Day, Event listed from 7–11 a.m.; check race-start and check-in details. **Where:** Tradition Square, Port St. Lucie. **Admission:** Check registration details.

The ninth annual Turkey Trot offers families a way to begin Thanksgiving with movement and community before heading home for dinner. Runners and walkers should check the event page for registration requirements, race timing and any fees rather than assuming the 7 a.m. event opening is the starting gun.

[Event details](https://traditionfl.com/events/turkey-trot-5k-2/).

## 12. Christmas on Main Street in Stuart

**When:** Friday, Nov. 27, 4–7 p.m.. **Where:** Riverwalk Stage and historic downtown Stuart. **Admission:** Free admission.

The holiday season gets a lively start with the 27th annual Christmas on Main Street. Stuart Main Street lists Santa and Mrs. Claus photos, artificial snowfall, sleigh rides, arts and crafts, live performances, treats and the lighting of a 30-foot Christmas tree. It's one of the strongest all-ages options of the whole break, and families can enjoy the downtown atmosphere without paying admission.

[Event details](https://stuartmainstreet.org/events/christmas-on-main/).

## 13. The Night After Thanksgiving Holiday Market at Tradition

**When:** Friday, Nov. 27, 4–9 p.m.. **Where:** Tradition Square, Port St. Lucie. **Admission:** Check organizer; purchases extra.

If the family isn't ready to go home after the Thanksgiving leftovers, Tradition is hosting an evening market with local vendors, food trucks and live music. The extended hours make it a flexible stop for browsing and grabbing dinner while kicking off the holiday shopping season.

[Event details](https://traditionfl.com/events/the-night-after-thanksgiving-holiday-market/).

## 14. Behind-the-Scenes Aquarium Tour in Fort Pierce

**When:** Saturday, Nov. 28, 2–2:30 p.m.. **Where:** St. Lucie County Aquarium, 420 Seaway Drive, Fort Pierce. **Admission:** Check aquarium admission and tour details.

Go beyond the public exhibits for a look at the equipment that keeps the aquarium's living ecosystems healthy. The short laboratory tour introduces visitors to filtration, lighting and other systems that support marine habitats. It's a good fit for curious school-age children who enjoy science; check availability and participation requirements first.

[Event details](https://visitstlucie.com/event/behind-the-scenes-tours-at-the-aquarium/2026-11-28/).

## 15. Rock'n Riverwalk in downtown Stuart

**When:** Sunday, Nov. 29, 1–4 p.m.. **Where:** Riverwalk Stage, downtown Stuart. **Admission:** Check event details.

Close out the long break with an afternoon of live music beside the St. Lucie River. Stuart's regular Riverwalk concert provides a casual final outing before school resumes, with restaurants and the downtown waterfront close by. Bring what you need to be comfortable outdoors, and check the city listing for any weather-related changes.

[Event details](https://www.stuartfl.gov/calendar.aspx?EID=5788).

**Before you go:** Dates, weather plans, age restrictions and registration availability can change, particularly around Thanksgiving. Check the organizer links before heading out, and verify holiday opening hours for venues with recurring programs. For additional activities in Martin, St. Lucie and Indian River counties, visit the [Treasure Coast Today events calendar](https://treasurecoast.today/events.html).
